title: Negotiable throughput clauses and operational SLA appendix for Dedicated capacity
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description:
Background:
Redwood Dedicated customers often ask for measurable throughput guarantees but differ on how to express them in contracts (tokens/min, requests/sec, or p95 latency under a target RPS). Legal and Sales need a negotiable appendix that maps customer needs to operational controls (autoscale rules, burst buffers, queueing) and a consistent, auditable credit model.

Proposal summary:
1) SLA primitives: define three orthogonal primitives that compose a Dedicated throughput commitment:
   - Serve Target: a tokens-per-minute (TPM) or requests-per-minute (RPM) target that represents normal expected steady-state throughput for the dedicated fleet.
   - Availability Corridor: a quantile-driven measurement (example: 95th-percentile TPM measured in 1-minute buckets over a rolling 30-day window) that defines the corridor where full-service is expected.
   - Degradation Banding: if observed throughput falls below the corridor, classify the severity into bands (Minor: 90-95% of target, Major: 70-90%, Critical: <70%) that map to credit levels and operational remediation steps.

2) Error budget and credit math (operationally auditable):
   - Measurement unit: tokens*minutes (tokens emitted aggregated per 1-minute bucket). Use customer-specific target_TPM as baseline.
   - Compute per-day deficit D_day = sum(max(0, target_TPM - observed_TPM_bucket) for each minute bucket in day).
   - Monthly error_budget_percentage = clamp( (sum(D_day over 30 days) / (target_TPM * 60 * 24 * 30)) , 0, 1 ).
   - Credit formula (example): credit_amount = monthly_invoice * min(0.5, error_budget_percentage * severity_weight) where severity_weight = 1.0 for Major, 1.8 for Critical, 0.4 for Minor. Caps and floors negotiable per contract.
   - Rationale: tokens*minutes aligns billing units with observable carrier capacity and is robust to burstiness.

3) Autoscale / Fleet controls (contractually-binding controls):
   - Autoscale interlock: Dedicated agreements can include an autoscale policy template that defines minimum and maximum GPU pools, warm-up time, and a burst allowance (X minutes per day at +Y capacity). The contract references the named template (e.g., Autoscale Template B - warm 8m, burst 10% for 15m/day).
   - Prioritization lanes: provide optional prioritized queues for guaranteed customers with configurable preemption policy (soft-preempt, hard-preempt). Contracts must enumerate whether lower-tier traffic is evicted during capacity stress.
   - Failover stance: agreement can require cross-AZ failover attempts before crediting, or explicitly waive failover for on-prem installs. Language must be explicit.

4) Observable & audit requirements (what we must ship):
   - A dedicated SLO dashboard per-customer showing 1-minute TPM buckets, rolling quantiles, and current band assignment.
   - Immutable measurement export (CSV or signed daily digest) that can be attached to credit disputes.
   - Automated credit calculation job that publishes proposed credits to billing queue with trace links to the minute-level data.

5) Contract language snippets (negotiation-friendly):
   - Service Commitment (example): "Redwood will provision Dedicated Serving capacity configured to meet a Serve Target of [X] tokens/minute. Redwood measures Served Throughput in 1-minute intervals and guarantees that the 95th percentile of these intervals across a rolling 30-day window will be no less than 95% of the Serve Target, subject to the exclusions below."
   - Credit trigger (example): "If the measured Served Throughput falls below the corridor described above, Customer will be entitled to a service credit computed in accordance with the agreed credit formula. Service credits are the sole and exclusive remedy for throughput degradation under this Appendix."
   - Autoscale appendix (example): "The Parties will adopt Autoscale Template [A|B] which defines warm-up, burst allowance, and max-pool behavior. Redwood will not be held liable for deficits outside of the configured template behavior."

Trade-offs and open questions:
- Measurement window: 30-day rolling window smooths noise but delays detection; shorter windows increase volatility. Proposed default: 30-day with optional 7-day fast-detection for operational alerts.
- Metric choice: tokens vs requests. Tokens better for generative workloads; requests for classification. Contract should allow either with conversion factor clause.
- Credit optical: fixed-percentage caps simplify legal negotiation but may over/under compensate for customer economic loss. Preference: percentage-based cap with ability to convert to token-hour credits for large enterprise customers.

Operational runbook (high level):
- Detection: SLO job emits alert when 7-day fast-detection shows >2% breach probability or rolling 30-day crosses a band.
- Triage: on-call engineer (Dedicated infra) owns first 30 minutes; escalate to Platform SRE at 60 minutes if not remediated.
- Mitigation ladder: 1) autoscale increase (if allowed), 2) activate burst buffer, 3) temporarily reroute compatible requests to fallback model variant, 4) coordinated failover.
- Postmortem: <72h hot write-up, full blameless postmortem within 7 days for Major/Critical.

Deliverables for this ticket:
- Finalized contract appendix text (legal-approved) - target 2 rounds of review with Sales/Legal.
- Implementation plan for minute-level measurement export and automated credit job (ENG owners assigned).
- Autoscale template library and mapping to contract templates.
- Dashboard for per-customer SLA telemetry.

Success criteria (accepted by PM/Legal/ENG):
- Contract appendix signed off by Legal and Sales (approve language and caps).
- Engineering spec merged (GH PR) to produce the measurement export and credit job.
- Dashboard demo with three internal customers and sample data.
- Automated credit calculation produces reproducible result for a synthetic failure scenario.

acceptance_criteria: Legal approves final appendix language and signs off on credit caps and exclusions.
ENG merges infra PR that publishes authenticated 1-minute TPM buckets for Dedicated fleets.
Billing automation consumes credit job output and can apply credits to a sandbox invoice.
SLO dashboard reflects rolling 30-day quantiles and Per-Customer band assignment for three test customers.
